bands.name: Not a standard yet
bands.note: Start with Sort and Set in order in one zone. Make one corner right before you widen.

bands.name: Gaps
bands.note: The standard exists in places. Close the weakest S before you add anything new.

bands.name: Good, hold it
bands.note: Hold it through the handover and the audits, and watch for the first slip.

bands.name: World class, sustain
bands.note: Sustain is the work now: leaders walk, the team owns the standard.

pillars.name: Sort
pillars.meaning: Clutter hides problems and eats space. Sort decides what belongs here and removes the rest.
moves: Walk the area with red tags: anything not used this week gets a tag, a date and a decision.
Clear one zone completely today instead of the whole area a little.
Agree where tagged items wait and who decides within seven days.
pillars.question: What is here that nobody has touched in a week?

pillars.name: Set in order
pillars.meaning: A place for everything saves the searching that makes shifts slow and tempers short.
moves: Mark the home of the ten most used items first: tape, floor marking, label.
Put consumables at the point of use with a visible min/max.
Photograph the standard and post it where the item lives.
pillars.question: Can a new starter find it in 30 seconds without asking?

pillars.name: Shine
pillars.meaning: Cleaning is inspection: a clean area shows leaks, damage and wear before they stop the work.
moves: Give every surface and machine one owner and one moment in the shift.
Fix the source of the dirt (a torn seal, a wrap station) instead of cleaning it again.
Report what cleaning finds: lights, leaks, loose guards.
pillars.question: What did cleaning find this week, and who fixed it?

pillars.name: Standardize
pillars.meaning: Without a visible standard every shift invents its own, and the score swings with the people.
moves: One picture of “good” at the area entrance, agreed with the team.
Make deviation obvious: shadow boards, colour codes, a line that must not be crossed.
Put the area check into the handover so it is seen twice a day.
pillars.question: How does a visitor see within a minute that something is wrong here?

pillars.name: Sustain
pillars.meaning: Sustain is the leader's part: audits that happen, actions that close, attention that is felt every week.
moves: Fix the audit day and the auditor pair for the next six weeks.
Close the last audit's actions before opening new ones.
Show the trend on the board and name what improved and who did it.
pillars.question: When did a leader last comment on this area's order?

pillars.name: Safety
pillars.meaning: A safety deviation is the loudest 5S finding: it says the standard is not held when it matters most.
moves: Clear exits, extinguishers and first aid today, before anything else.
Walk the forklift and pedestrian routes at peak time and watch where they cross.
Discuss the last near miss at the next briefing.
pillars.question: Where did someone nearly get hurt here in the last month?

pillars.name: Security
pillars.meaning: A security gap costs more than the item lost: trust, time and investigations.
moves: Lock the high-value zone and log access from today.
Check doors and gates at shift start and end, and name who does it.
Move personal items to lockers; nothing personal in the goods flow.
pillars.question: Who was in the locked zone yesterday, and how do you know?

pillars.name: Satisfaction
pillars.meaning: People hold a standard they helped make; a tired, unheard team lets it slip.
moves: Answer every raised 5S problem within a week, even with a no.
Fix the ergonomics of the heaviest task first.
Name a good result on the board and say who did it.
pillars.question: What did the team ask for last month, and what happened to it?

sort: Only items needed for today's work are in the area; nothing parked “for later”.
No broken equipment, empty pallets or waste standing in aisles or at the dock.
Every doubtful item carries a red tag with a date and a decision.
Documents and labels on the walls are current; nothing outdated or duplicated.
set: Every tool, cage and trolley has a marked home, and it is there now.
Floor markings for pallets, walkways and staging lanes are complete and visible.
Shelves and locations are labelled so a new starter finds anything in 30 seconds.
Consumables (tape, labels, wrap) are at the point of use with a min/max level.
shine: Floors are clean and dry; no spills, dust or wrap scraps.
Forklifts, scanners and scales are clean and checked, with the inspection sheet filled in.
The cleaning schedule shows who cleans what and when; today is signed off.
Leaks, damage and broken lights are reported, not worked around.
standardize: The 5S standard of the area is posted as one picture of what “good” looks like.
Everyone on shift can say what they are responsible for keeping in order.
Visual controls (shadow boards, min/max, colour codes) make deviations obvious at a glance.
The handover checks the area's state; deviations go on the shift board.
sustain: 5S audits happen on schedule, and the last three results are on the board.
Actions from the last audit are closed or have an owner and a date.
Leaders walk the area and comment on 5S at least weekly.
The team updates the standard itself when the work changes.
safety: Emergency exits, fire extinguishers and first-aid kits are free and signed.
Pedestrian and forklift routes are separated and respected.
The PPE of the area is worn, and the rule is visible.
Near misses in the area are recorded and discussed.
security: High-value and controlled goods are in a locked, labelled zone with access logged.
Doors and gates to the yard are closed and controlled during the shift.
Nothing personal (bags, phones) is stored in the goods flow.
Visitors and contractors are signed in and escorted.
satisfaction: The team can raise a 5S problem and sees it answered within a week.
Rest area, water and lighting meet the standard the team agreed.
Ergonomics: heavy items at waist height, no repeated reaching above the shoulder.
Good 5S results are shown and named on the board.

sort: The desk and back office hold only what today's shift needs; no old flyers or spare devices.
The housekeeping store has no unlabelled chemicals, broken items or expired amenities.
The kitchen has no expired goods, duplicated utensils or broken equipment in use.
Every doubtful item carries a red tag with a date and a decision.
set: Keys, cards, cash and forms each have one marked place at the desk, and are there now.
Linen and amenities are shelved by type with labels and min/max levels.
Kitchen tools and ingredients are stored by station; nothing on the floor.
Guest-facing printed materials are current and in their holder.
shine: Lobby, desk and back office are clean; no cables, dust or cups in view.
Housekeeping trolleys and store shelves are clean and restocked at shift end.
Kitchen surfaces, floors and drains are clean; the cleaning plan is signed off today.
Defects (lights, locks, leaks) are reported in the system, not left for the next shift.
standardize: The desk setup and the trolley setup are shown as one picture of “good”.
Everyone knows which checks belong to their shift: cash, safe, logbook, fridge temperatures.
Visual controls: colour-coded cloths and chemicals, labelled shelves, par-level cards.
The handover checks the state of the area and logs deviations.
sustain: 5S audits run on schedule and the results are on the staff board.
Actions from the last audit are closed or have an owner and a date.
The duty manager walks front office, store and kitchen weekly and comments on 5S.
The team changes the standard when the work changes: new amenities, a new PMS screen.
safety: Emergency exits, extinguishers and evacuation plans are free and visible.
Wet-floor signs, non-slip mats and safe knife storage are in use.
Chemicals are stored locked with the safety data sheets at hand.
Near misses and guest incidents are recorded and reviewed.
security: Cash drawer, safe and key cabinet are locked; access is logged.
Guest data on printouts and screens is not visible to other guests.
Back-of-house doors are closed and badge-controlled.
Lost property is logged, labelled and stored locked.
satisfaction: The team can raise a problem at the desk, in the store or in the kitchen and sees an answer within a week.
Staff room, water and breaks meet the agreed standard.
Ergonomics: trolleys roll, shelves are reachable, no lifting above the shoulder.
Good results and guest compliments are shown and named on the board.

sort: Only today's routes and carts are in the staging lanes; nothing from yesterday.
No broken carts, empty totes or waste in the sorting area or at the dock.
Every doubtful item carries a red tag with a date and a decision.
Posted route sheets and notices are current; old ones are gone.
set: Every route has a marked staging lane and the carts stand in it.
Totes, bags and carts have a marked home and return to it after the wave.
Scanners, chargers and labels are at the point of use with a min/max level.
Van parking bays are numbered and match the route board.
shine: Floors and dock plates are clean and dry; no tape scraps or packaging.
Carts, totes and scanners are clean and checked; defects are tagged.
The cleaning schedule shows who cleans what and when; today is signed off.
Yard lighting, barriers and markings are intact, and reported when not.
standardize: The sort and dispatch standard is shown as one picture at the lane.
Everyone on the wave knows their lane, their checks and their end-of-wave tasks.
Visual controls (lane colours, cart counts, departure clock) make a late lane obvious.
The wave handover checks the area's state and logs deviations.
sustain: 5S audits run on schedule and the last three results are on the board.
Actions from the last audit are closed or have an owner and a date.
The station lead walks the floor and comments on 5S at least weekly.
Drivers and sorters propose changes to the standard, and some are adopted.
safety: Walkways and van lanes are separated; reversing is guided.
Exits, extinguishers and first aid are free and signed.
Hi-vis and safe footwear are worn; the rule is visible.
Near misses in the yard and on the floor are recorded and discussed.
security: High-value parcels are in a locked cage with access logged.
Yard gates are closed; vans are locked when unattended.
No personal items in the goods flow; lockers are used.
Visitors and partner drivers are signed in.
satisfaction: Sorters and drivers can raise a problem and see it answered within a week.
Water, toilets and the rest area meet the agreed standard.
Ergonomics: heavy parcels at waist height, carts that roll, no stacking above the shoulder.
Good results and good catches are shown and named on the board.

tips: Audit what you see, not the SOP.
Score the floor as it is this minute. The document says what should be; the audit says what is.
Score the floor, not the people.
A 2 is a gap in the system, not a verdict on the shift. Say so before you start.
Anything at 2 or below gets a note and an owner. Scores without actions are decoration.
Audit the same areas on the same weekday in the same order. A trend needs equal measurements.
Not sure whether it belongs here? Tag it with a date. The decision follows within a week.
